W6 after E063 (crash). Time ≈ 0.1 s fixed + steps × per-step cost. Tip E061: 5.0235 s, 0.7534 on seeds 0–2 (225 steps, unselected population mean ~0.7532).

Biggest misses: E062 (Muon→SGD cost 2.9 pp and saved 0.28 s) and E056/E052/E059/E061 time misses of ±0.1 s. Common thread: I underestimated how load-bearing per-step update quality is (Muon, GELU smoothness, stem work) and mis-modelled time at about ±0.1 s, which is my noise floor and not a signal.

Mechanisms:
1. Accuracy rises with optimizer steps at about 0.8–1.5 s/pp. Cuts of epochs, steps or samples trade near that dial (E020, E031, E041, E045, E048, E061).
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail carries accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Late backward truncation saves more than its MAC share, since it skips BN/GELU backward and optimizer traffic. It is free only after a block has finished learning (E028, E036, E046, E049 free; E037, E054, E055 costly).
4. Per-step quality dominates. SGD −2.9 pp (E062), ReLU −0.54 (E056), stride-2 stem −1.1 (E051). Swaps in activation, optimizer or stem structure are far from neutral and mostly negative.
5. Averaging variants, LS late, warm-up, Lookahead interval and BN recalibration are null or negative. wd ×0.5 gave about +0.2 pp. The recipe is near a local optimum with respect to cheap scalar tweaks.
6. Noise: the 3-seed mean moves ±0.2 pp across rebuilds of the same commit. Time moves ±0.05–0.1 s. The 20-seed rebuild SD is ≲0.06 pp. Winner's curse is 0.05–0.15 pp.

Unsure: whether Muon lr/momentum are mis-tuned (the only untested near-free booster), how much of the freeze cost is anneal vs detach, whether the recipe is under-fit, and the PCIe offset.

Expectations: the activation swap saves little, since tanh-GELU moves the same bytes. Muon lr/momentum are coin flips with a small expected gain and a risk of loss. The freeze-anneal tweaks are near neutral. The Muon-merge systems change saves ≲1%.

forecasts.reason: Tanh-GELU/SiLU move the same bytes; the projected saving is likely under 1.5%, so the gate closes with no run and no accuracy gain.
The LR floor is mostly irrelevant under averaging; any effect is within the noise.
The gain is probably 0.05–0.15 pp for +0.09 s, near break-even with the dial.
The lr ×1.5 effect is small and its sign is uncertain; E014 saw +0.09 pp at 3 seeds.
Overhead saving is plausible at about 1%, but bf16 batched NS may shift the numerics slightly.
Higher momentum over 225 steps with Lookahead probably slows adaptation slightly; a small loss is more likely than a gain.
Diagnostic with no recipe change; train top-1 will likely be well under saturation (~80–90%) given heavy LS and 9 epochs.

cruxes: Is Muon lr or momentum mis-tuned for this 225-step regime? A ≥0.12 pp gain at unchanged time would fund about 0.1 s of trims.
Is the rebuild SD of the 20-seed mean really ≲0.06 pp, so that sub-0.1 pp decisions are resolvable?
Is non-NS optimizer and launch overhead at least 1% of train time (I107), and is the early 20 px phase still free below 225 steps?
